decision: The final test period is 2021-10-01 to 2021-12-31, the same quarter as in Project 1. Its rows are dropped right after the start time is parsed, and only their count is kept.
evidence: The file covers 2019-12-31 21:27 to 2021-12-31 23:52; the last full quarter holds 80,081 of 441,077 rows (18.2%), and the earlier quarters stay for development.

decision: Public holidays and adjusted working days are known future information and enter the calendar as two flags.
evidence: 61 holiday days and 13 adjusted working days in 2020-2021, all published by the State Council months ahead (notices of 2019 No. 16, 2020 No. 27 and the January 2020 Spring Festival extension).

decision: Only rows that cannot be placed in an hour of the study period, rows outside the three districts and exact duplicates are removed; inconsistent but placed sessions are kept, because each one started at a post.
evidence: 17 rows removed (all of them before 2020-01-01), 360,979 kept, 80,081 held out; repeated user, post and start time: 0; other time field unreadable: 0; end before start: 0; payment before end: 72,006; order created after start: 205,028; numeric field unreadable: 0; negative energy or amount: 0; zero energy delivered: 46,052; weather outside physical range: 0.

decision: A data gap is a network run of 24 or more hours with no session; gap hours stay in the series with a flag and are left out of training, scoring and the MASE scale. Every other zero is real zero demand.
evidence: 0 gap hours; the longest network run without a session is 12 hours (from 2020-02-13 23:00); from 2020-04-01 the share of zero hours is network 0.4%, Tongxiang 2.1%, Xiuzhou 6.5%, Nanhu 15.0%.

decision: MASE is scaled with the daily seasonal naive forecast, m = 24.
evidence: From 2020-04-01 the autocorrelation at 24 hours is above that at 168 hours at every level (network 0.848 against 0.821, Tongxiang 0.788 against 0.748, Xiuzhou 0.662 against 0.642, Nanhu 0.590 against 0.581), and the in-sample seasonal naive MAE is lower with m = 24 (network 7.12 against 7.63 sessions per hour).

decision: Holidays, the Spring Festival included, are kept as legitimate variation and described to models by the holiday and adjusted working day flags; no day is removed.
evidence: From 2020-04-01, network demand on holidays is 0.99 times that of normal weekdays and 0.91 times on adjusted working days; the 2021 Spring Festival week averaged 327 sessions per day against 504 (-35%).

decision: Training rows start on 2020-04-01, which confirms the Project 1 boundary; January to March 2020 serve only as lag history.
evidence: Network sessions were 6,217 in January 2020, 1,391 in February and 6,392 in March, and 11,136 in April; the February collapse belongs to the first COVID-19 restrictions and not to the demand the models must learn.

decision: Weather stays an exogenous candidate: a model may use it only as a daily forecast known at issuance, and Task 2 tests whether it helps.
evidence: Weather is recorded once per day and district; from 2020-04-01 its Spearman correlation with daily network demand is +0.62 for temperature, +0.04 for humidity and +0.01 for precipitation; rainy days have 0.98 times the sessions of dry days.

decision: Forecasts are issued once a day at 00:00 with the data up to the hour starting at 23:00 of the previous day, for the 24 hours of the issuance day; horizon h is clock hour h-1.
evidence: Daily planning needs one forecast per day; at midnight the same hour of the previous day is known for every horizon, and that lag has autocorrelation 0.848 at network level (Section 5.3).

decision: The 24 values come from a direct strategy with one shared model: one row per (issuance, level, horizon), inputs known at 00:00 only, hour of day as an input, no forecast fed back as an input.
evidence: The layout gives 52,608 development rows; 24 separate models would each see 1/24 of them, and a recursive forecast would feed its own errors into later hours of the day (Ben Taieb et al., 2012).

decision: 13 inputs are included, weather is a candidate and 6 groups are excluded; each is labelled historical, known future or exogenous.
evidence: Every included target-anchored lag is at least 24 hours, every issuance-anchored window ends with the hour starting at D-1 23:00, and make_forecast_rows asserts for every row that no input reads an hour at or after the issuance.

decision: Models are compared on the four expanding-window folds of Project 1, training from 2020-04-01 and validating on one quarter each; no purge gap, because sessions are counted by start hour and nothing crosses a boundary.
evidence: Validation issuances 92, 90, 91, 92 (365 in total); training issuances 183, 275, 365, 456; 2021-Q1 contains the Spring Festival.

decision: The primary score is MASE averaged over the 24 horizons, then over the 4 levels with equal weight, then over the 4 folds, reported with its per-fold values; MAE and RMSE per level are secondary scores in sessions per hour.
evidence: MASE has no unit, so Nanhu (mean 4.4 sessions per hour) weighs as much as the network (26.4).

decision: mean_4w is the reference baseline: every later model must beat its primary score on the same folds; the other two baselines are reported beside it.
evidence: Primary MASE snaive_day 1.000, snaive_week 1.047, mean_4w 0.869; per fold for mean_4w: 0.854, 0.782, 0.829, 1.012.
